questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very sure of the fact that I wanted to go on an exchange this semester, the destination wasn't as important for me. The most important factor for me was the possibility to try to experience studying in an international context. When I learnt that my good friend from my studies planned on going to Prague in Czechia, it was a no-brainer that we could plan on going together.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a nice experience, however there were some unexpected cultural shocks regarding the study structures.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The student system was a little bit difficult to navigate, considering the fact that some of the teachers used another system (Moodle) and barely updated the former student system. Some had a Moodle page, but didn't update that, and some even just used google docs for information. It was however easy to find the campus and classes, even though most of the staff didn't speak English.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were signed up for a tour around campus on our first day of school, however we couldn't find the tour guides at all, even though we were there earlier. Apparently this was due to a miscommunication error, however it was quite disappointing. However, the International Office at Charles University were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Actually it was my roommate who found the housing. It didn't seem to be that difficult, however we also booked our apartment long before arrival. We used the website Erasmusu.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no issues in living off campus, in fact most of the dormitories offered by the University were a lot further away from campus. We lived right in he middle of the city, so we had easy access to most places in Prague. However, there is a very good public transportation system in Prague so there is no need to worry wherever you stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dormitories looked very bad on the pictures, and it really seemed like you either won or loss the lottery wherever you were stationed. Some dormitories were crazy far away, and just were overall bad, but some dormitories I visited were really great. There were even some students who got single rooms, however this wasn't certain.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had some issues with the course registration which were very stressful, however it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office was quick and effective when answering all of our questions, and they did so in the best way they could.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not very successful at all. I was only able to register for two out of five classes that I had wanted to begin with. And one of them I even had to write to the professor to be sure to get into, since I was put onto a waiting list. One class apparently wasn't available for exchange students, which seemed weird, since it was accepted by the host university. It was only more frustrating as I was actually registered the course before getting kicked out again and having to find an alternative solution. Another class had been removed from when I first looked for classes until registration.
It would have been a lot easier if we were notified which courses were a part of the full time students schedules, so we could steer around those, since they were full even before we could register. The registration was such a stressful process, even though I started registrating as soon as the option opened.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you register for backup courses regarding the courses you need credits for in your home University.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was messy, some of the teachers were not proficient in their English skills. There was no connection between ECTS points and the curriculum/exams. Some of the exams were extremely easy while others demanded more energy than expected. It was just one big circus.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was generally quite low, which came as a surprise to me

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was just chaotic. I'm used to very structured teaching in UCPH, but it seemed like the teachers decide their own structure at Charles University, which made it confusing and all out terrible in some cases. It was also difficult having to concentrate for 80 minutes straight without a break.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU Institutions
Promoting Democracy Abroad: The US and the EU in Third Countries
European Economic Integration
Anthropology of the EU
Comics as a Medium

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: EU Institutions was great for getting to know the institutions in the EU, however there were a lot of anecdotes so be aware of that. Promoting Democracy Abroad: The US and the EU in Third Countries was a very nice course with a pedagogical and outspoken teacher. The teacher in European Economic Integration was very knowing and taught us a lot. I would not recommend Anthropology of the EU at all. Comics as a Medium was probably my favourite course, however it wasn't very academic.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, it was all quite cheap. I did however order a lot of takeaway, since it was so cheap, which spiked my food budget a lot.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation was crazy cheap. Around 120 dkk for three months free transportation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really partake in many of the opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No clue, I didn't really look into it. It wasn't really advertised that blatantly however.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try to partake in the events in the introweek. It was filled to the brim, but I think you could just show up nonetheless. It seemed like it was nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for trips around Czechia. The train tickets are exceptionally cheap, and Czechia is such a beautiful country. You could go to Cesky Krumlov and Brno for example. You could also visit the surrounding countries since the tickets are that cheap. This is what most students do.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to feel a part of the city, but Prague is also very touristy. As long as you drank beer you belonged.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Partake in the events by the student organisations in the introweek, that is how I got to know local students. Other than that it seemed like an impossible task to be honest.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of people didn't speak English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cheap beer, beautiful city and parks, cheap and very good public transport and the fact that Czech people are usually not all up in your business, which suits me well as a Dane.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to find friends outside of your classes too, since you don't get any breaks, so it's difficult to get to know them.
Don't be afraid of living in the dorms, the ones I saw looked very nice (although they were quite far away), it's very cheap, and it's an easy way to get to know people. Also, you can always switch dorms if you'd like.
Don't expect to be challenged academically. Use it as a well-earned easier semester.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the International Office if you need help. They're great. A lot of the other offices in Prague are not very helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience living in another country and getting to know another culture. You almost felt like a local by the end of it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to figure out what you needed to fill out, how to register and the sorts. People who have been on an exchange earlier are usually very good at helping out however.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your exchange!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
